rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and identify poorly resolved pairs while aiming to elute all 10 compounds near the 10-minute scoring threshold. The midpoint temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction.

Change only gradient duration to test whether the crowded central peaks respond to a shallower slope. The last peak should remain near or below 10 minutes, leaving room to improve resolution without a time penalty.
Keep the improved gradient and raise temperature by 5 °C to test selectivity at the sole unresolved pair. Higher temperature should also shorten retention, preserving the zero time penalty.

The critical pair converged strongly between 40 and 45 °C; testing 55 °C may carry it through an elution-order reversal into adequate separation. Extrapolation suggests the other pairs should retain sufficient resolution while the last peak stays below 10 minutes.

Slightly steepen the gradient at 55 °C: the earlier slope test suggests this should widen the critical pair after its temperature-induced order reversal. The other pairs appear to have enough resolution margin, making this a promising route to CRF 1.0 with a shorter run.

Preserve injection 5’s gradient slope of 0.075 organic fraction per minute while trimming the unused high-organic portion. All peaks should elute before the shortened gradient ends, retaining CRF 1.000 with a shorter programmed gradient.

Raise the gradient window by 0.05 while preserving the successful slope and temperature to test whether elution can be accelerated without losing full resolution. Injection 5 remains the maximum-score reference; this run probes a shorter alternative.

With the maximum CRF already secured, test a substantially faster gradient at 60 °C. The combined slope and temperature changes may reverse and separate the converging middle pair while shortening the run; the low starting organic fraction protects early-peak retention.

Lengthen the fast 60 °C gradient to test whether the two crowded middle pairs gain sufficient separation. This isolates the slope effect at 60 °C while targeting a fully resolved run shorter than the established maximum-score method.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with a slope close to injection 9 to shift selectivity in the remaining critical pair. This explores a substantially shorter fully resolved method, while checking that the early peaks retain adequate separation.

Explore lower-temperature selectivity with the same gradient as injection 5, since the faster high-temperature methods introduced new overlaps. This tests whether the central cluster can be fully separated on a different temperature branch while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Use a slightly shallower gradient to recover the middle-pair resolution lost in injection 7 while retaining its higher starting organic fraction. This should keep the last peak below 10 minutes and may provide another maximum-score method with more balanced resolution margins.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope from injection 12 to increase the resolution margin of its closest pair. The other critical pair changed little with slope, so this may retain CRF 1.000 with better minimum resolution and a last peak still below 10 minutes.

Combine a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient to balance the two limiting middle pairs. This tests whether the minimum resolution can improve while preserving full separation, adequate early retention, and a last peak below 10 minutes.

Reduce the slope slightly from injection 14 to lift its sole unresolved pair above R = 1.5. The other critical pair has some margin, and the last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially restoring CRF 1.000 with improved minimum resolution.

Use a slope between injections 14 and 15, closer to the fully resolved injection 15. This should retain CRF 1.000 and stronger resolution margins than injection 5 while slightly shortening elution relative to injection 15.

With CRF 1.000 already secured, explore the low-temperature boundary for a potentially faster fully resolved alternative. Cooling may separate the near-coeluting central peaks seen at 30 °C by changing their elution order, while the shorter gradient limits retention time.

Test a substantially shallower gradient at 60 °C to carry the remaining middle-pair overlap through its slope-dependent order reversal. This may yield full resolution with greater separation margins while keeping the last peak near, but below, 10 minutes.

Revisit the promising 40 °C selectivity with a shallower slope to separate its limiting central pair, while raising the starting organic fraction to offset the added retention. This tests a different route to full resolution below 10 minutes, with the established CRF 1.000 methods retained as references.

Shift injection 19’s gradient window upward while preserving its slope and temperature to shorten retention. This tests whether the fully resolved 40 °C method tolerates a higher starting organic fraction without compromising its central or early pairs.

Make injection 20’s gradient slightly shallower to recover resolution of its sole limiting pair. The last peak is expected to remain below 10 minutes, potentially restoring the maximum CRF at this higher starting organic fraction.

Reduce the slope slightly from 0.045 to 0.04375 per minute to lift injection 21’s limiting pair above R = 1.5. The projected last-peak time remains below 10 minutes, making this a targeted test for another maximum-score method.

Preserve the successful slope and temperature of injection 5 while further trimming the unused gradient tail. The last peak previously eluted at approximately 0.57 organic fraction, so all peaks should remain within this gradient and retain CRF 1.000.

Test a faster gradient at the successful 55 °C temperature to establish the speed limit for full resolution. This may compromise the middle pair, but directly checks whether a shorter maximum-score method exists while retaining injection 23 as the proven reference.

Preserve the proven 0.075-per-minute slope through the first nine peaks, then hold at 0.50 organic fraction to test a shorter programmed gradient and lower final solvent strength. The isolated last peak will elute during the hold; if it remains below 10 minutes, this method should retain the maximum CRF of 1.000.
